name: Santa Maria Maggiore
basis: existing church; DBpedia geo:lat/long (en.wikipedia), matches gcatholic plus code 8FMHQ7F3+84 (43.7733,11.2528)
note: Faces Piazza di Santa Maria Maggiore at corner of via de' Cerretani (it.wikipedia). Cross-check: https://gcatholic.org/churches/italia/50703

name: Chiasso de' Buoi
basis: no fetched source locates this lane
note: Document places it in the popolo of Santa Maria Maggiore (heirs' palagio there). Lane not identified in any fetched source; do not plot except as within the parish of Santa Maria Maggiore (43.77327, 11.253067).

name: San Lorenzo
basis: existing basilica; en.wikipedia infobox coords, matches gcatholic plus code 8FMHQ7F3+WR (43.7748,11.2546)
note: Cross-check: https://gcatholic.org/churches/italy/0072

name: Borgo San Lorenzo
basis: midpoint of its two ends: it.wikipedia says it runs between Piazza San Giovanni and Piazza San Lorenzo; Baptistery 43.7731,11.255 (en.wikipedia) and San Lorenzo 43.774917,11.253861 (en.wikipedia)
note: Florence street, NOT the Mugello town. Name attested from 1117; originally opened only onto via dell'Arcivescovo, reaching Piazza San Giovanni only in the 1800s. Endpoint sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florence_Baptistery ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_San_Lorenzo,_Florence

name: Via de' Fossi
basis: modern Via de' Fossi is outside the San Lorenzo parish; identification with the document's street unconfirmed
note: it.wikipedia: today's Via de' Fossi runs from Piazza Santa Maria Novella to Piazza Goldoni (Piazza Goldoni 43.770925,11.24775 per en.wikipedia; S. Maria Novella basilica 43.7746,11.2493), named probably from a ditch (fossato) along the second (Dante-era) walls. That is in the Santa Maria Novella/Ognissanti area, not the popolo of San Lorenzo. If the document puts it in San Lorenzo, it may be a different 'via de' fossi' (e.g. along a moat/ditch near San Lorenzo); left unplotted.

name: Gomito dell'Oro
basis: no fetched source mentions this place-name
note: Document places it in the popolo of San Lorenzo; web searches found nothing.

name: Spedale di San Giovanni fra l'Arcora
basis: no fetched source locates the hospital
note: Document: 'fuori delle mura allato allo spedale di san Giovanni' near San Lorenzo, i.e. outside the walls on the San Lorenzo side. Searches (it.wikipedia church lists, catalogues) found no location for San Giovanni fra l'Arcora; left unplotted.

name: San Firenze
basis: position of the present Chiesa/Complesso di San Firenze from gcatholic plus code 8FMHQ795+W4 (decoded); the Baroque complex stands on Piazza San Firenze where the medieval parish church was
modern_name: Complesso di San Firenze, Piazza San Firenze
note: it.wikipedia: complex lies on Piazza San Firenze between Borgo dei Greci, via dell'Anguillara and via Filippina (https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complesso_di_San_Firenze). Medieval church replaced by the 17th-18th c. complex, so the point is the site, not the 1380s building.

name: Borgo de' Greci
basis: it.wikipedia says the San Firenze complex is bounded by Borgo dei Greci; point = San Firenze (gcatholic plus code)
note: Street runs west from Piazza San Firenze toward Piazza Santa Croce; point marks its San Firenze end only.

name: San Piero Maggiore
basis: church demolished 1783/84; stood on the site of today's Piazza San Pier Maggiore (theflorentine.net); coordinates from DBpedia (en.wikipedia San Pier Maggiore, Florence)
note: Three portico arches survive at the piazza edge. Site source: https://www.theflorentine.net/2015/10/01/the-church-of-san-pier-maggiore/

name: Via di San Gilio
basis: it.wikipedia: Via Sant'Egidio was formerly 'Via San Gilio'/'di San Giglio', named from the church of Sant'Egidio (now in Ospedale di Santa Maria Nuova); point = Sant'Egidio church, gcatholic plus code 8FMHQ7F5+8W (decoded)
note: Point is the street's western end at Piazza Santa Maria Nuova; the street runs east toward the San Pier Maggiore area. it.wikipedia adds that the old name also covered today's via Maurizio Bufalini. Coordinate source: https://gcatholic.org/churches/italia/50697

name: San Simone
basis: existing church on Piazza San Simone; DBpedia geo (en.wikipedia), matches gcatholic plus code 8FMHQ796+X4 (43.7699,11.2603)
modern_name: Chiesa dei Santi Simone e Giuda
note: Now Ukrainian Greek Catholic. Cross-check: https://gcatholic.org/churches/italia/50791

name: Via del Palagio
basis: it.wikipedia: Via Ghibellina was originally 'via del Palagio del Podestà', the stretch from the Bargello to the old Porta Ghibellina (now via Verdi); point = midpoint of Bargello (43.77037,11.25835) and Teatro Verdi (43.769951,11.261023), both DBpedia
modern_name: Via Ghibellina (Bargello to via Verdi stretch)
note: Runs just north of San Simone, consistent with the popolo. Endpoint sources: http://dbpedia.org/resource/Bargello ; http://dbpedia.org/resource/Teatro_Verdi_(Florence)

name: San Bartolo del Corso
basis: lost church; no fetched source locates it
note: Presumably on or near today's Via del Corso, but the it.wikipedia Via del Corso page and church lists do not mention it; not plotted.

name: Via di San Martino
basis: no fetched source identifies the medieval street
note: Likely named from San Martino del Vescovo (it.wikipedia 'Chiese di Firenze': in piazzetta di San Martino near via de' Magazzini), but no source equates a modern street with 'via di San Martino'; not plotted.

modern_name: Chiesa di San Michele a Castello

note: castellitoscani.com also places San Niccolò inside the castle: https://castellitoscani.com/en/calenzano-castle . Calenzano comune point 43.867,11.167 (en.wikipedia).

modern_name: Pieve di San Martino, Sesto Fiorentino

name: Barberino
basis: town; en.wikipedia coords 43°32'N 11°10'E (low precision, ~1 km)
note: Identified as Barberino Val d'Elsa, not di Mugello: Spoiano and San Jacopo a Magliano are Val d'Elsa/Val di Pesa places (see those entries).

name: San Bartolomeo (Barberino)
basis: church San Bartolomeo a Barberino d'Elsa; gcatholic plus code 8FMHG5VC+7X (decoded). Approximate because identification of the popolo with this church is inferred
modern_name: Chiesa di San Bartolomeo, Piazza Barberi, Barberino Val d'Elsa
note: Another San Bartolomeo (a Palazzuolo) exists in the comune (btfinearts.it), so identification is not certain.

name: Santa Lucia (Barberino)
basis: not securely identified
note: Candidate: Chiesa di Santa Lucia al Borghetto (Franciscan, Tavarnelle side, attested 1260; it.wikipedia Tavarnelle Val di Pesa), but no source ties it to Barberino's popolo; not plotted.
